1. e5 {The pawn, one move.} Rb6 {The rook, at its queen's knight's third square. (a) NOTE: By
keeping that line with his rook, he hinders your king from advancing; and if he were to desert
that line before you had pushed your pawn, he would lose the game, as will be seen by a back-
game. 26.6} 2. Ra7 {The rook, at the adverse queen's rook's second square.} Rc6 {The rook, at
its queen's bishop's third square (b) 3.1 NOTE: He ought not to depart from this line with his
rook, but at the very instant when you shall push your pawn.} 3. e6 {The pawn, one move.} Rc1
{The rook, at the adverse queen's bishop's square. (c) NOTE: If he had given check, he would
have lost the game.} 4. Kf6 {The king, at the adverse king's bishop's third square.} Rf1+ {The
rook gives check, at the adverse king's bishop's square. (d) NOTE: He must continue to give you
check, in order to drive you away from your pawn; and, at the very moment when your king falls
upon his rook, he will attack and take your pawn.} *
